title: Exposure lamp error
shortDescription: Scanner exposure lamp failed to provide correct brightness.
fullDescription:
SC101 is logged when the Ricoh scanner lamp does not produce the expected light level during the pre-scan calibration. The scanner uses a white strip under the glass to check brightness; if it reads too low, SC101 is raised.

Common causes are a dirty white reference strip, a failed lamp, or a dirty scanner mirror. On newer LED-based scanners, a dead LED array triggers the same code.

Cleaning is the first step; replacement of the scanner lamp unit is done by a technician.

fixSteps.title: Clean scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Clean the scanner glass and the white strip just under the edge.

fixSteps.title: Replace lamp
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces the scanner lamp assembly.

whenToCallPro: After cleaning if the code remains.

faq.a: Yes; printing is not affected by SC101.

title: Machine serial number error
shortDescription: Serial number not programmed or lost from NVRAM.
fullDescription:
SC195 indicates the main machine serial number is missing from NVRAM. It occurs after controller board replacement without NVRAM transfer or NVRAM corruption.

A technician uses SP mode to rewrite the correct serial number from the machine label.

This error is benign on boot but blocks billing/counter functions.

fixSteps.title: SP mode serial write
fixSteps.instruction: Technician enters SP5-811 and writes correct serial number.

faq.a: On the label on the back of the machine.

title: Polygon motor error
shortDescription: Laser polygon motor did not lock to target speed.
fullDescription:
SC202 indicates the Ricoh laser polygon motor did not reach or maintain its lock signal. The polygon spins the mirror that sweeps laser across the drum.

Worn bearings, dust in the LSU, or a failed scanner motor PCB cause this. Ricoh recommends LSU replacement rather than motor-only repair.

The error is detected during the polygon spin-up phase.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Power off 60 seconds; may temporarily clear.

fixSteps.title: Replace LSU
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces laser scanner unit.

faq.q: Can I clean the LSU myself?
faq.a: Not recommended — contamination risk.

title: Polygon motor error (Color)
shortDescription: Color laser unit polygon motor fault.
fullDescription:
SC320 is the color-printer equivalent of SC202: the polygon mirror motor inside the color LSU did not lock to the required speed. A single LSU may serve all four colors or one per color depending on model.

Consistently returning SC320 after a power cycle signals a failed motor assembly.

The LSU must be replaced by a technician with proper alignment.

fixSteps.title: Power off/on
fixSteps.instruction: Let the machine sit powered off for 2 minutes, then restart.

fixSteps.title: LSU replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Technician installs new color LSU.

faq.q: Can I print in black and white?
faq.a: Often no — Ricoh color LSU failure usually stops the machine entirely.

title: Development motor error
shortDescription: Developer unit motor stalled or failed to reach speed.
fullDescription:
SC390 is logged when the motor driving the developer roller fails. Without development motion toner cannot be charged and transferred to paper.

The fault is usually a failed motor or drive gear. On machines nearing end of life, the developer unit itself may have seized.

After motor replacement the developer bias and density should be recalibrated in SP mode.
symptoms: Light or missing prints before fail

fixSteps.title: Inspect developer
fixSteps.instruction: Technician rotates developer by hand to check resistance.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new motor and recalibrate in SP mode.

faq.q: Does SC390 block the entire machine?
faq.a: Yes, printing is halted.

title: Image transfer bias leak
shortDescription: High voltage transfer leak detected.
fullDescription:
SC440 indicates a leakage current in the image transfer high-voltage circuit. The transfer roller applies a bias to pull toner from the drum onto the paper or transfer belt.

Moisture, a worn transfer roller, or a failed HVPS can leak this voltage, triggering SC440.

Drying in a warm environment helps if moisture is the cause; persistent SC440 requires HVPS or transfer unit replacement.

fixSteps.title: Dry out machine
fixSteps.instruction: Leave the printer powered off in a dry room for 24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Replace transfer unit
fixSteps.instruction: Technician installs new transfer unit.

whenToCallPro: After drying if the error persists.

faq.a: Yes; above 70% RH increases risk.

title: Drum temperature sensor error
shortDescription: Drum thermistor reading out of range.
fullDescription:
SC495 flags a drum temperature sensor whose reading is outside valid range. Ricoh monitors drum temperature to compensate image density.

A disconnected or failed thermistor, or an aged drum with the sensor compromised, can trigger this.

Technician reseats connectors first, then replaces the thermistor or drum unit.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Technician checks thermistor harness for looseness.

faq.a: No, but continued operation may cause density issues.

title: Fusing lamp thermistor open
shortDescription: Fuser thermistor reading no temperature rise.
fullDescription:
SC541 is one of the most common Ricoh errors. It means the fusing thermistor reads no or very slow temperature rise when the fuser lamps are powered.

Causes include a blown fuser lamp, an open thermistor, tripped thermal fuse, or a failed AC drive board.

Ricoh requires SP5-810 reset after the fuser or thermistor is replaced.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Technician swaps the fuser unit with a known good one.

fixSteps.title: SP5-810 reset
fixSteps.instruction: Enter SP5-810 to clear the fusing error latch.

faq.q: Can I reset SC541 without fixing?
faq.a: SP5-810 will reset but will return immediately if hardware is faulty.

title: Fusing warm-up timeout
shortDescription: Fuser did not reach ready temperature in time.
fullDescription:
SC542 is logged when the fuser does not reach ready temperature within the timeout period. The lamp is working but insufficient to warm the sleeve.

Common causes: weak lamp output from age, low mains voltage, or a partially failed lamp filament.

Replace the fuser assembly and clear with SP5-810.

fixSteps.title: Check mains
fixSteps.instruction: Verify voltage with socket tester.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Technician installs new fuser.

faq.a: Cold rooms make SC542 more likely on marginal lamps.

title: Fusing overheat
shortDescription: Fuser temperature exceeded safe limit.
fullDescription:
SC543 indicates the fuser overheated — the thermistor reported a temperature above the safety threshold. The machine locks to prevent damage.

Usually caused by a failed triac keeping the lamp on, or a shorted thermistor.

Do not reset until the underlying fault is found — continued operation risks fire.

causes.cause: Stuck triac on AC drive board

fixSteps.title: Power off immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Keep printer off until inspected.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose
fixSteps.instruction: Technician checks triac and thermistor.

faq.a: No, investigate first.

title: Fusing temperature drop
shortDescription: Fuser temperature fell below target during printing.
fullDescription:
SC552 is logged when the fuser cannot maintain its target temperature during a print run. The lamp pulses cannot keep up with heat loss into paper.

Heavy card stock or high-volume runs exacerbate the issue, but a failing lamp or thermistor is usually the root cause.

Fuser replacement is the standard fix.

fixSteps.title: Move to dedicated circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure no heavy loads share the outlet.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Technician swaps fuser.

faq.a: Heavy stock accelerates the fault if the lamp is already weak.

title: Controller start-up error
shortDescription: Main controller did not respond to engine board.
fullDescription:
SC672 is the classic Ricoh 'stuck boot' error: the main controller did not respond to the engine within the boot window. The operation panel displays SC672.

Causes include corrupt firmware, a loose controller-to-engine cable, or a failed controller board. Many cases resolve with a simple power cycle or cable reseat.

If firmware corruption is suspected, reflash is required via SD card.

fixSteps.title: Hold power off
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug machine for 5 minutes, then restart.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Technician reseats the controller-engine cable.

fixSteps.title: Reflash firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Use SD card with matching firmware to reflash.

whenToCallPro: If power cycle and reflash fail.

faq.a: No, many cases are cable-related.

title: Engine start-up error
shortDescription: Engine board did not respond at start.
fullDescription:
SC670 is the inverse of SC672 — the controller is up but the engine did not respond. Wiring between boards or engine board failure is typical.

Basic troubleshooting is cable reseating. If unresolved, the engine board is replaced.

fixSteps.title: Cable reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Technician reseats engine board connectors.

faq.a: Rarely — SC670 is usually hardware.

title: Finisher error
shortDescription: Optional finisher motor or sensor failure.
fullDescription:
SC720 covers finisher faults — stapler, sorter, or paddle issues. The exact sub-code refines the cause (SC720-01 stapler, SC720-02 paddle, etc.).

Check the finisher for jams or staple remnants first. If clear, the finisher drive motor or sensor needs service.

User-level jam clearing resolves many SC720 events.

causes.cause: Jam or staple stuck in finisher

fixSteps.title: Open finisher
fixSteps.instruction: Remove stapler cartridge and clear any stuck staples.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall stapler
fixSteps.instruction: Seat cartridge and close cover; run test job.

whenToCallPro: If clearing jams does not fix.

faq.a: Yes, just disable finishing in the driver.

title: Energy saver mode error
shortDescription: Machine could not transition to energy-save state.
fullDescription:
SC816 is a soft error logged when the machine's energy saver mode transition fails. Often triggered by firmware bugs or stuck sub-board communication.

A reboot typically clears it. Persistent SC816 may call for a firmware update.

The machine usually remains operational but with SC816 shown on the panel.

fixSteps.title: Reboot
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle the MFP.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Apply latest Ricoh firmware.

faq.a: No, cosmetic more than functional.

title: Kernel error
shortDescription: Fatal controller software exception.
fullDescription:
SC819 is a kernel-level software error on the Ricoh main controller. It indicates the controller firmware encountered an unrecoverable state and halted.

Reboot and firmware reflash are the main responses. If it recurs under specific job conditions, logs should be collected for Ricoh support.

Hardware failure (RAM, NVRAM battery) can also trigger it.

causes.cause: Firmware exception from bad job data

symptoms: SC819 after a specific print job

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the power button to cold-boot.

fixSteps.title: Firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Install latest firmware.

fixSteps.title: Replace controller
fixSteps.instruction: If hardware fault suspected, technician replaces controller board.

whenToCallPro: If reflash does not clear recurring SC819.

faq.a: Yes, pending jobs may be lost.

title: Software performance error
shortDescription: Application-level software error.
fullDescription:
SC899 is a Ricoh software error typically raised by the application stack (e.g., SmartSDK apps, embedded scanning). Compared to SC819 it is recoverable and does not halt the whole device.

Restarting the affected application or rebooting usually clears it.

Repeated SC899 may point to a specific add-on app that needs reinstallation.
symptoms: SC899 when launching a specific app

fixSteps.title: Restart app
fixSteps.instruction: From Web Image Monitor, stop and start the app.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall app
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reinstall the SDK application.

faq.a: No, usually only the app is affected.

title: Software operation error
shortDescription: Unexpected operation condition.
fullDescription:
SC990 is a catch-all for unexpected software conditions on Ricoh MFPs. The system detected an inconsistency during operation that does not map to any specific sub-code.

A power cycle typically clears it. Reoccurrence with the same job suggests problematic print data.

Collect the job details and report to Ricoh if it persists.

fixSteps.title: Reboot
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle the machine.

fixSteps.title: Print test page
fixSteps.instruction: Try a simple test document to confirm stability.

faq.a: Usually transient; monitor if it repeats.

title: Print job error
shortDescription: Job could not be processed.
fullDescription:
SC995 occurs when a specific print job fails to process. Reasons include unsupported PDL commands, oversized jobs, or incompatible paper settings.

The machine remains operational; the job is dropped. Reprint from a simpler source to test.

Log the job characteristics if it repeats.

fixSteps.title: Update driver
fixSteps.instruction: Install current Ricoh PCL or PostScript driver.

fixSteps.title: Simplify job
fixSteps.instruction: Split large jobs or reduce resolution in driver settings.

whenToCallPro: Only if driver update does not help.

faq.q: Do I need more RAM in the printer?
faq.a: Only for very large PostScript jobs; rare.

title: Application selection error
shortDescription: Selected application failed to start.
fullDescription:
SC997 is raised when an application from the home screen (copy, scan, fax, app) cannot launch. Memory shortage or corrupted app state is the usual cause.

Rebooting frees memory and typically clears it. If reoccurring, disable recently installed SDK apps one-by-one to isolate the culprit.

If hardware-related the controller board may need service.

causes.cause: Memory exhaustion from too many apps

symptoms: SC997 when tapping copy or scan

fixSteps.title: Reboot
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle to free memory.

fixSteps.title: Disable SDK apps
fixSteps.instruction: From Web Image Monitor disable non-essential apps.

whenToCallPro: If reboot and app disable do not help.

faq.a: No; stored jobs and address book persist.
